arcade_identity.basis: The current-ROM audit found a shared 60-callback elapsed updater and four per-record selector counters, but the traced $4717-$4787 consumer updates $61C4-$61C7 values subsequently consumed by enemy route-choice logic at $42F4-$4306. This is not proof that those bytes are pose IDs or that one shared pose clock controls the player, roaming, den/release, death, attract, or instruction actors. Exact audited ranges, byte identity, and limits are in arcade-owner-audit.txt.

arcade_clock_owner_findings.exact_behavior: The main loop decrements $61B6; on wrap it reloads $3C, increments $61B7, and decrements four bytes at $61CE-$61D1. The $4717 routine is gated by $61B6==$3B, round-robins a counter via $61D2&3, and reloads it from a DIP/elapsed-indexed table at $47AE or $47CD. It derives per-record $61C4-$61C7 values from four active records at $602C with stride 5. $42F4-$4306 reads those values in route selection.
arcade_clock_owner_findings.finding: Shared elapsed scheduling is proven for this enemy route-selection state only; pose-clock sharing and actor-family sharing are not proven.
